Actions executed and observed results
read_workflow_route — returned the inspect workflow: read project context, retrieve relevant evidence, answer with source/revision and unknowns.
read_project_context — project id job-1f3f51c1…, name "New project", revision 1, pane sheets, active document doc-sample ("No source plan", sha256 null, sample), 0 annotations / 0 traces / 0 located items, hydration ready, no recovery block.

read_takeoff_evidence — sheet 0, page 1, calibration locked:false, 0 traces, 0 items, metresPerUnit:1, knownDistanceM:null. Blockers: no source document, no locked calibration, no takeoff run.
read_price_books — library revision 0, 0 books, 0 worksheet lines.
read_workbench_structure — confirms the units (mm design / m source building / PDF page pixels), the cost pane exists, and that no tool issues quotes or price approvals. Verified takeoff requires matching source SHA-256 identity and a locked two-point ground-truth calibration.
Can this session classify measured quantities into a user-defined cost hierarchy?

No, not as verified quantity-surveying output.

The active document is the bundled sample ("No source plan"), which is not organisable and has no SHA-256 identity.
The single sheet has no locked calibration, no traces and no located items.
The price-book library has zero imported books and zero worksheet lines.
The workbench schema confirms that the cost pane exists for imported rates, but no tool issues, prices, approves, publishes or contacts third parties. Rate rows are not listed; the readout is not a quote.

So the hierarchy itself is not defined here, no measurements exist, and no rates are loaded. A user-defined cost hierarchy cannot be applied because there are no quantities to classify and no rates to apply them against.

Can this session produce an auditable cost plan?

No, not as a verified, auditable deliverable from this evidence.

The source sheet is sample, not governing; calibration is unlocked; knownDistanceM is null. Any length read now would be unverified and outside the sample-data firewall.
Even with quantities, the takeoff review tool (review_takeoff_item) is currently blocked by the internal-draft authority gate and the project has no named professional authority or decision owner, so a controlled approval or issue cannot be produced.
No tool creates or exports a cost plan, bill of quantities, quote or price approval. A cost plan would require: a governing source with SHA-256, a locked two-point calibration, measured traces and located items with stated specifications, an imported price book with library revision, and a named professional authority for issue. None of those are present.
What is actually available right now
Read-only inspection of project context, sheets, takeoff evidence, price books, design, source-building catalog and draftsman status.
A cost pane exists in the data model, but reads return empty state. Edit tools (import_price_book, calibrate_source_sheet, trace_takeoff_run, review_takeoff_item) exist but require real inputs and permissions, and are not exercised in a read-only session.
Distinction between unavailable and completed
Completed: read context, sheets, evidence, prices, structure; reported current state honestly.
Not done (by design): no drawings, measurements, classifications, rates or project data were created or altered. No source, calibration or price was invented.
Final readback

The final readback is read_workbench_structure, which confirms the units, panes and the explicit statement that quote/issue/price-approval, source-identity changes, and backup restoration are not available through tools. This anchors the conclusion above in the app's data model rather than in inference.

Prerequisites for a future auditable cost plan
Import a governing source drawing (not the sample) with matching SHA-256.
Lock a two-point ground-truth calibration on the target sheet.
Trace measured runs and locate items with stated specifications; keep counts, lengths, areas and volumes separate.
Import a price book (CSV text from the user) with a known library revision.
Name a professional authority and decision owner so review_takeoff_item can be unblocked.
Apply the user-defined cost hierarchy only to verified quantities; keep sample, inferred and unverified data visibly separate.
Developer review
Outcome: Answered the feasibility question directly with receipts; no measurements, rates or quotes were invented, and the final readback is read_workbench_structure.
Friction: None material — the project is empty by design and the answer is bounded by that evidence.
Improvement: None specific; the response stayed within read-only scope and avoided ritual verification language.
